title: Smooth hover suppression and icon-cluster hitbox alignment
creator: Maya Patel
description: Problem: Several product teams have reported subtle regressions where icon-only buttons in dense toolbars have inconsistent hover flicker, misaligned hitboxes between visual outlines and pointer targets, and opaque hover suppression when rapid cursor movements cross adjacent controls. These issues are pronounced in high-contrast themes and when token overrides (density / spacing tokens) are applied at the app layer. This ticket scopes a design-led remediation that standardizes token mapping, introduces a smooth hover-suppression interaction pattern (debounced fade + kinetic micro-gesture), and defines a hitbox alignment contract for icon clusters to avoid accidental activations and restore keyboard/focus parity.
acceptance_criteria: Icon-only buttons across desktop toolbar, compact lists, and card controls have consistent pointer hitboxes that match the defined interactive area in visual specs (no more than 6px misalignment on any axis).
Hover state uses a 60ms suppression debounce then a 120ms fade-in for hover affordance; rapid cursor passes (<60ms) should not trigger visible hover flicker.
High-contrast and dark themes map spacing/touch tokens correctly so hover overlays and focus rings do not overflow neighboring controls.
Keyboard navigation exposes the same focus visuals as pointer hover (focus-visible parity), and focus restoration after a pointer-initiated press-cancel returns to logical focus.
Design tokens required (spacing, hitbox-offset, hover-debounce, hover-fade-duration) are documented in the token catalog and example token overrides are provided.
Cross-team regression tests (visual snapshot + a11y keyboard flow) added to the component suite and passing in the designlib playground.
design_notes: We observed three classes of failures: visual offset between SVG icon bounds and CSS interactive padding; immediate hover-on/hover-off flicker when moving between tightly spaced icons; and focus ring clipping in high-contrast themes where ring thickness exceeds token-provided padding.

Proposed interaction: apply a small pointer "safe area" of 6px around icon visuals as the canonical hitbox, independent from visual padding. Implement hover suppression by ignoring enter/leave events shorter than hover-debounce token (60ms). Use opacity transitions for hover surfaces to avoid layout jank.

Accessibility: ensure focus-visible always shows after keyboard tab regardless of hover suppression. For users with reduced-motion preference, reduce fade to an instant state transition and skip debounce when assistive tech is detected.
proposed_solution: Component change: make hitbox computed from token; visuals (background, shadow) remain inside existing padding. Update CSS logical properties so RTL works naturally.

Transition plan: roll out tokens as a nonbreaking opt-in in designlib 2026.03, provide migration guide for applications that previously relied on custom padding overrides. Add a temporary compatibility flag (prefers-legacy-hitbox) for early adopters.

visual_specs: Canonical hitbox: icon visual bounds + --button-hitbox-offset on all sides; visual background remains 8px inset from hitbox in default density.
Hover surface: semi-transparent overlay with 0.06 alpha in light theme, 0.12 in dark theme; subject to hover-fade token.
Focus ring: uses --button-focus-ring-padding and matches accessible color tokens for each theme variant.
qa_checklist: Validate hitbox alignment across 4 screen densities (100%, 125%, 150%, 200%).
Confirm hover suppression prevents visual flicker for <60ms passes and still triggers for steady hover >60ms.
Keyboard tab focus shows focus-visible same as hover overlay and returns correctly after press/cancel.
Reduced-motion preference disables fade but keeps suppression semantics.
Visual snapshots match approved Figma comps for default and high-contrast themes.
